missing_info: Full uv --verbose output for the failing run, not just the DEBUG excerpt
Contents of pyproject.toml and the src/ layout, to confirm the package name and entrypoint mapping
Whether the .pth file in .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages is present and whether it carries the macOS hidden flag (ls -lO)
Whether the project lives in an iCloud-synced Desktop folder
Confirmation that a fresh venv outside Desktop works, to isolate the environment
external_evidence: uv logs 'Requirement already installed: work==0.1.0 (from file:///Users/.../Desktop/work)' yet the generated .venv/bin/work script fails at 'from work import main'. This means the editable install's .pth path link is not being applied at import time, which points to Python or the OS skipping the .pth file, not uv's install step. Related issue 16977 documents Python skipping hidden .pth files on macOS, and the project sits under ~/Desktop, where iCloud sync can set the hidden flag. Not verified from the report alone.

possible_duplicates.reason: Same symptom on macOS: a local editable package becomes unimportable while uv reports it installed, attributed to Python skipping hidden .pth files, which is the likely mechanism here.
macOS ModuleNotFoundError on 'uv run <project>' for a uv init project, tied to a venv file under iCloud-synced storage; a similar environment-level cause.

rationale: The reporter labels this a bug, and I keep the type as bug because uv reports the package as installed when the import path is broken. The decisive clue is that the install is correct per uv's own cache heuristic: the docs (cache.md) say local directory editables are only rebuilt when pyproject.toml changes, and touching the file forces a rebuild, so this matches documented behaviour. The failure lies in the .pth link not being honoured at import time, which points to macOS or Python (hidden .pth files, plausibly from the Desktop/iCloud location) rather than uv. Search found 16977 and 9902 with the same macOS ModuleNotFound pattern. Needs an MRE with verbose output and a .pth/hidden-flag check before any action.
